items.title: Arrests planned when ISIS-linked families land in Australia
items.description: Flights have been booked for families linked to Islamic State fighters returning from Syria to Australia, with women in the group facing arrest and investigation when they touch down.

items.title: Australia's emergency fuel stockpile to increase under multi-billion dollar plan
items.description: More than $10 billion will be spent bolstering Australia's fuel security as the federal government attempts to shield the nation from the long-term consequences of the war in Iran.

items.title: Royal commission 'appalled' by man in swastika shirt near hearing
items.description: It comes as the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion enters its third day of hearings from Jewish Australians sharing lived experience.

items.title: Cancellation 'disaster' for business that expected Inland Rail for 25 years
items.description: Regional communities from Queensland to Victoria react after the major federal rail project was axed overnight.

items.title: Residents of camp where newborn died say they have 'nowhere else to go'
items.description: Long-term campers set up at the base of a levee popular with walkers are asking people to have an "open mind" about why they are there, saying many have nowhere else to go.

items.title: Live: Trump says plan to move ships through Hormuz to pause for possible peace deal
items.description: US President Donald Trump says Project Freedom, aimed at opening the Strait of Hormuz, will pause to try to get a peace deal signed with Iran. Follow live.

items.title: Iran maintains Strait of Hormuz blockade with 'annoying' mosquito fleet
items.description: Iran's so-called mosquito fleet of small, speedy attack boats has become an increasingly aggressive nuisance for the US Navy, as it attempts to break the blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Child protection workers stood down over Kumanjayi Little Baby reports
items.description: Three child protection workers have been stood down and a department-wide review ordered over its handling of a series of child protection reports about Kumanjayi Little Baby.

items.title: Live: Australian dollar surges past four-year high, ASX rally tops 1pc
items.description: The local share market and currency are both strongly higher. Follow the day's events and insights on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Ban on Craig Silvey's books hardened in public schools after guilty plea
items.description: WA Education Minister Sabine Winton confirms a temporary ban on Silvey's books being used as texts in public schools will now be made permanent.

items.title: Cruise of a lifetime becomes nightmare after hantavirus outbreak
items.description: It was meant to be the journey of a lifetime for Boston travel influencer Jake Rosmarin, crossing the south Atlantic Ocean on the MV Hondius, but the trip has turned into a nightmare after three people died in a hantavirus outbreak.

items.title: More than 500 turtles discovered on the outskirts of far west NSW town
items.description: Hundreds of turtles are thriving near an outback NSW town, only months after the lake where they live was on the verge of drying up.

items.title: Tim Picton's alleged attacker avoids immediate jail over separate charge
items.description: Brodie Jake Dewar had admitted assaulting another man two days before he allegedly struck Mr Picton, who later died in hospital.

items.title: Man fighting removal to Nauru loses High Court challenge
items.description: A man fighting plans to remove him to Nauru loses his High Court challenge, after the government's deal to have the island take in people released from indefinite immigration detention is upheld.

items.title: How a flamboyant thief quietly pulled off an extraordinary coin heist
items.description: David Gee pulled off one of the most baroque and ambitious coin heists in Australian history, nicking precious coins from the special collections of the nation's oldest library without anybody noticing.

items.title: The ideal age to start swimming lessons for your child
items.description: Swimming ability is declining in Australia, and experts say knowing the right age to enrol your children in lessons — as well as what to do if you can't access them — is key to improving water safety.

items.title: Meet the artist turning Venezuelan protest music into art
items.description: Unable to return to her homeland, Melbourne-based artist Nadia Hernández has reconnected with her culture through art.

items.title: Scientists discover species of ancient 'dimpled' koala in WA
items.description: A new analysis of fossilised koala skulls and bones has revealed an extinct species of koala lived in WA until a few thousand years ago.

items.title: More than 8 million Australians now receive income support
items.description: The number of people accessing income support payments has risen by 2 million in the past decade, with more Australians unable to work due to deteriorating mental and physical health.

items.title: Labor axes funding for $45b Inland Rail project linking Melbourne to Brisbane
items.description: The federal government has halted plans for the Melbourne to Brisbane Inland Rail, amid concerns the project could cost more than $45 billion to complete.

items.title: Three men walked into a whisky bar. Eight years on, a court case has ended
items.description: The Salamanca Whisky Bar was accused of selling fake versions of the award-wining Sullivans Cove whisky. But eight years after the saga began, a court in Hobart has dismissed the charges.

items.title: Qld government backs proposal for zip-line over Brisbane River
items.description: A Queensland developer has proposed to build a wheelchair-accessible zip-line to cross the Brisbane River from Kangaroo Point to the City Botanic Gardens.

items.title: How climbing is trying to remain inclusive after IOC's trans ban
items.description: For Phoebe and Luce, joining an LGBTQI+ social climbing group was transformative. But as a trans woman and non-binary person, they have faced barriers to participating in elite competition and are calling for change.

items.title: 'Justice is served': Afghan women's footballers react to FIFA ruling
items.description: A FIFA rule change has allowed the Afghan women's football team to compete in official internationals for the first time since the Taliban took over in 2021. Mina Ahmadi says the victory is a "very emotional" one for the team.

items.title: Rahm pays fine to return to DP World Tour as LIV doubt grows
items.description: Jon Rahm will be eligible for Europe in next year's Ryder Cup after agreeing to pay fines and play events on the DP World Tour this season, a move that also triggered speculation about his future with LIV Golf beyond 2026.
